{{Short description|British chemist (born 1959)}}
[[File:AKPowell.jpg|thumb|Prof. Annie K. Powell]]
'''Annie K. Powell''' (born October 20, 1959) is a British scientist and a professor of inorganic chemistry at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] (KIT), Germany.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |date=2011 |title=Annie Powell |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.201005774 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=50 |issue=4 |pages=800 |doi=10.1002/anie.201005774 |bibcode=2011ACIE...50..800. |issn=1521-3773|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Her research focuses on [[Single-molecule magnet|single-molecule magnets]], coordination clusters, metal–organic frameworks ([[Metal organic framework|MOFs]]), [[Environmental chemistry|environmental]] and [[sustainable chemistry]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Annie K Powell Group |url=https://www.aoc.kit.edu/powell/index.html |access-date=2025-10-16 |website=www.aoc.kit.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Powell was born in [[Lincoln, England|Lincoln]], [[England]],<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Annie K. Powell |url=https://www.aoc.kit.edu/powell/akpowell.html |access-date=2025-10-16 |website=www.aoc.kit.edu}}</ref> the daughter of Stephen and Elisabeth. She attended Mount Street, Westgate, and Yarborough schools in Lincoln. Powell earned a Bachelor of Science degree with honours in chemistry from the [[University of Manchester]] in 1981. She received her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in chemistry from the same university in 1985, under the supervision of Dr. Mike Ware, for research on complexes of iron(III).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Magnetic Nanoscale Materials and Exotic Spin Structures: A 65th Birthday Gift to Annie K. Powell |url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/magnetochemistry/special_issues/8JF2IS703U}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
After receiving her doctorate, Powell worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Freiburg]] in Germany with Prof. Dr. H. Vahrenkamp from 1986 to 1988. In 1988, she joined the [[University of Kent]] at [[Canterbury]], UK, as a lecturer. Later, from 1989 to 1999, she worked in different roles as lecturer, senior lecturer, reader, professor of chemistry at the [[University of East Anglia]], [[Norwich]] in the UK. Since 1999, she has been a full professor (W3) at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] (formerly the University of Karlsruhe).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /> 

While working at the [[University of East Anglia]], Powell, along with her colleague S. Heath, synthesized an Fe(III) molecule containing 19 iron centres. Subsequently, through collaboration with Dante Gatteschi of the [[University of Florence]], the magnetic properties of this molecule were measured, revealing a large spin ground state. Further studies established that the system behaves as a [[single-molecule magnet]] (SMM).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Powell |first1=A. K. |last2=Heath |first2=S. L. |last3=Gatteschi |first3=D. |last4=Pardi |first4=L. |last5=Sessoli |first5=R. |last6=Spina |first6=G. |last7=Del Giallo |first7=F. |last8=Pieralli |first8=F. |date=1995-03-01 |title=Synthesis, Structures, and Magnetic Properties of Fe2, Fe17, and Fe19 Oxo-Bridged Iron Clusters: The Stabilization of High Ground State Spins by Cluster Aggregates |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00114a012 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=117 |issue=9 |pages=2491–2502 |doi=10.1021/ja00114a012 |bibcode=1995JAChS.117.2491P |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref> She contributed to the discovery of the first molecule exhibiting a toroidal moment.<ref name=":1" /> The non-collinear arrangement of Ising spins in a Dy<sub>3</sub> triangular coordination complex is considered an early example in the development of the research area known as Single Molecule Toroics (SMTs).<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Tang |first1=Jinkui |last2=Hewitt |first2=Ian |last3=Madhu |first3=N. T. |last4=Chastanet |first4=Guillaume |last5=Wernsdorfer |first5=Wolfgang |last6=Anson |first6=Christopher E. |last7=Benelli |first7=Cristiano |last8=Sessoli |first8=Roberta |last9=Powell |first9=Annie K. |date=2006 |title=Dysprosium Triangles Showing Single-Molecule Magnet Behavior of Thermally Excited Spin States |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.200503564 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=45 |issue=11 |pages=1729–1733 |doi=10.1002/anie.200503564 |pmid=16496432 |bibcode=2006ACIE...45.1729T |issn=1521-3773|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The Powell Research Group at [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology|KIT]] is currently engaged in research on molecular magnets, [[Metal–organic framework|MOFs]], [[biomimetics]], [[coordination compounds]] and multi functional materials.<ref name=":3" />
